excerpts: Thank you, Jenn, and good morning to everyone.
The combination of our investments, disciplined execution, and focus on clients is delivering improved returns and more durable results.
Services delivered its highest ever quarterly revenue and a return of over 30%.
This offset Rates’ lower performance.
Banking revenues climbed 34% led by a sharp increase in financing activity amidst an overall strong wallet.
We played a role in the majority of the top equity and debt issuances in the quarter, including lead roles on high-profile IPOs such as SpaceX and Cerebras.
As we enter the second half, the pipeline looks healthy.

Furthermore, our resilient customer base kept fueling underlying drivers – loan growth, higher spend and better credit performance than expected.

We continued to make progress in our transformation with a large body of work passing internal audit validation.
On the macro-front, the conflict in the Middle East has weighed a bit on global growth whilst giving inflation a second wind.

docs.title: Q1 2026 Earnings Call: CEO Prepared Remarks

excerpts: Thank you, Jenn, and good morning to everyone.
For the full year, our returns improved to 8.8%, a 180-basis point improvement after adjusting for Banamex and Russia, and adjusted net income surpassed $16 billion.
We continue to innovate to provide our clients with always-on, cross-border, multi-bank solutions.
In 2025, we integrated Citi Token Services with 24/7 U.S. dollar clearing, launched in Hong Kong and Dublin, and added euro as a transaction currency.
In October, we began the journey to a unified custody infrastructure and enabling near real-time asset servicing by launching Single Event Processing.
All the investments we have made have translated to growth and strong market share gains.
Markets delivered record revenues, even surpassing our 2020 performance.
Combined with better capital efficiency, RoTCE increased to 11.6%.
Citi had a role in 15 out of the 25 largest investment banking transactions of the year and advised Boeing, Pfizer, Nippon Steel, Mars, Johnson & Johnson, Blackstone and TPG.

It’s a direct result of the strategy we’ve executed over the past two years, attracting and retaining industry-leading talent and driving better operating efficiency that’s allowed us to invest in key growth areas.
USPB’s returns more than doubled for the year, reaching mid-teens, driven by continued product innovation, solid customer engagement and our high-quality card portfolio.

Branded Cards revenue grew 8% driven by robust engagement from customers in spend, borrowing and new account acquisitions across our proprietary offerings, and our American Airlines and Costco partnerships.
While Retail Services showed some revenue softness, the business’s returns remain solid.

With much of our transformation behind us, we are shifting our focus to how we can use AI tools and automation to further innovate, re-engineer and simplify our processes beyond risk and controls to improve client experience whilst reducing expenses.
With inflation now at normal levels globally, almost every central bank is becoming more accommodating.
China is relying on exports to grow and compensate for slower domestic consumer demand.
And Europe has taken some steps to accelerate its anemic growth, and we are hopeful that Germany can create a meaningful stimulus.
Our corporate clients are in great financial shape and, as you know, are predominantly investment grade in terms of credit quality.
But we aren’t taking any victory laps.
Gonzalo has big shoes to fill indeed.
